answer: A historical place that genuinely moved me was the Sixty Dome Mosque in Bagerhat, in the south-west of Bangladesh, which I visited during a trip to Khulna about three years ago. It dates back to the fifteenth century, and stepping inside felt like travelling back in time. The architecture was absolutely [[magnificent]], with thick brick walls and long rows of slender stone pillars supporting dozens of small, rounded domes. What struck me most was the sense of history embedded in the walls; you could almost feel the countless generations who had passed through. A local guide explained its [[significance]], telling us that it was built in the time of Khan Jahan Ali and that the whole area is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, which made the experience far richer than simply looking at old stones. I also wandered around the grounds and the large pond beside it, and I was surprised to learn that the mosque is still used for prayers today, so it is a living place rather than just a monument. I found myself genuinely [[awestruck]] by the craftsmanship of an era without modern machinery. Places like this are an important reminder of our [[heritage]], and I think it is vital that we preserve them, especially as damp and salt are a real threat to old brickwork in that region. Honestly, I came away with a deeper appreciation of the past and how much skill and devotion went into these monuments. It was easily one of the most memorable trips I have taken.

followUps.q: Would you recommend it to foreign visitors?
followUps.answer: Absolutely. It is one of the most important historical sites in Bangladesh, and combining it with a trip to the Sundarbans makes perfect sense, because both are in the same part of the country.

followUps.q: Did you learn about it at school?
followUps.answer: Yes, briefly, in our history lessons, but reading about it in a textbook is nothing compared to standing inside. Seeing it in person made the history feel real rather than just facts to memorise.

note: Named the real site (Sixty Dome Mosque, Bagerhat, 15th century, UNESCO) and corrected 'towering domes' to many small domes; added when, guide details, still in use, conservation.
